configuration.scope: Uniform mean columns derived from each sourced density/field pair and the assumed emitting path; both field signs are sensitivity cases. Intrinsic polarization RMS is the declared volume-averaged polarized emissivity times the full emitting path; normalized depth integration applies depolarization without a second horizon truncation. Angular structure and the two dispersions remain independent conditional assumptions, not inferred local priors.

separability.scope: Conditional examples at 1 K intrinsic polarization RMS at 30 MHz, with assumed local columns and angular statistics. Linear and PCHIP native-beam interpolants define a model comparison, not a measured fine-channel response. Gaussian visibility illustrations retain the complex relation and both sidereal phases. No detection significance is inferred.

horizon.scope: Conditional uniform-rate scenarios; no local screen statistics or polarized emissivity are measured here.
horizon.projection_status: Illustrative directions, not a field-orientation posterior.
horizon.emissivity_status: Illustrative unit normalization; multiply by the assumed local polarized emissivity.
horizon.spectrum_status: Illustrative power law; no absorption or turnover below 20 MHz.
horizon.path_status: Illustrative finite emitting volume, not a measured cloud extent.

scenarios.name: LIC_model26
scenarios.source_location: Slavin and Frisch 2008, Table 2 B0 and Table 5 n_e, model 26.
scenarios.status: One photoionization-model pair; extending B0 as a uniform local field is an additional assumption.

scenarios.status: Lower endpoint of the adopted density range; 1 microgauss field is illustrative, not measured by this source.

scenarios.source_location: Yeung et al. 2024, Section 4.2: adopted n_e=(4 +/- 0.5)e-3 cm^-3.

scope: Full signed uniform-mean sensitivity from the adopted density/field/path pairs. Dispersion and angular statistics remain conditional assumptions. Marginal variances contract the complete four-branch operator; phase coefficients and weights retain the joint C/J. Frequency/depth refinement bounds the full Q/U covariance change; angular and band-limit checks cover every reported marginal. The joint stage reconstructs any requested complete covariance.
